subject: maths
question:
Cylinder is surmounted by a cone at one end and a hemisphere at the other end. The common radius is 7 cm, the height of the cylinder is 6 cm and the total height of the structure is 32 cm. Find the volume (in cm³) of the structure. Use π=(22)/(7)​

2f
solution:
**Given:**

Radius (r) = 7 cm

Height of cylinder (h꜀yₗ) = 6 cm

Total height = 32 cm ⇒ Cone height (h꜀ₒₙₑ) + Hemisphere height (r) = 32 − 6 = 26 cm

⇒ Hemisphere height = r = 7 cm

⇒ Cone height (h꜀ₒₙₑ) = 26 − 7 = 19 cm

pi=dfrac{22}{7}

**Formula used:**

Cylinder: V = π × r² × h

Cone: V = dfrac{1}{3} × π × r² × h

Hemisphere: V = dfrac{2}{3} × π × r³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Cylinder: V꜀yₗ = π × 7² × 6 = π × 49 × 6 = π × 294

⇒ Using π = 22/7: V꜀yₗ = 294 × (22/7) = (294 ÷ 7) × 22 = 42 × 22 = 924 cm³

⇒ Cone: V꜀ₒₙₑ = (1/3) × π × 7² × 19 = (1/3) × π × 49 × 19 = π × (931/3)

⇒ Using π = 22/7: V꜀ₒₙₑ = (931/3) × (22/7) = 20482/21 cm³ = 975 1/3 cm³

⇒ Hemisphere: Vₕₑₘᵢ = (2/3) × π × 7³ = (2/3) × π × 343 = π × (686/3)

⇒ Using π = 22/7: Vₕₑₘᵢ = (686/3) × (22/7) = 15092/21 cm³ = 718 2/3 cm³

⇒ Total V = 924 + 20482/21 + 15092/21

⇒ 924 = 19404/21

⇒ Total V = (19404 + 20482 + 15092) / 21 = 54978/21 = 2618 cm³

**∴ Volume of the structure = 2618 cm³.**
